statement: How many of the letters in the word ZEBRA can be folded along a straight line so that the two halves match exactly?

choices.misconception: I only looked for up-and-down fold lines, and only A has one.
I only looked for fold lines going across, and found only E and B.
I counted Z because it looks the same when turned round, but turning is not folding.
I thought every capital letter has a fold line somewhere and counted all five.

hints: Try both kinds of fold: up-and-down and across.
Check each letter on its own. A fold line can go up and down or across the middle. A letter that only looks the same after turning it round does not count.
A folds up and down. E and B fold across the middle. Z only matches when it is turned round, and R does not match at all. Count the letters that fold.

solutions.reliable: Check each letter. Z: no fold line works, it only looks the same when turned halfway round. E: folds across the middle. B: folds across the middle. R: no fold works. A: folds up and down. So E, B and A can be folded, which is 3 letters. The idea to keep: test every letter for both up-and-down and across fold lines, and do not mix up folding with turning.

whyOnTest: Students must test two directions of fold and keep turning symmetry separate from folding symmetry, two classic traps.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
